findings.claim: The Zenodo version-link metadata uses a non-Zenodo relation value and points at the concept DOI instead of the prior version DOI.
findings.evidence: `related_identifiers[0]` is {identifier: 10.5281/zenodo.17899134, relation: isVersionOf, scheme: doi}. Zenodo's documented relation CV does not list `isVersionOf` (https://developers.zenodo.org/), and the repo's Zenodo generator uses `isNewVersionOf` against the prior DOI for new-version deposits.
findings.required_action: Replace this entry with a Zenodo-supported version-chain link to the prior release DOI, using `relation: isNewVersionOf`; keep the concept DOI in prose/citation if you still need to name the series-level DOI.

findings.claim: The operators subsection scopes the time-indexed operators to levels K1 and above on time slices of a fixed continuum K, but the K1 module itself says time does not exist at K1 and tau(K1) is undefined. Without an explicit clarification that t is only a formal evolution parameter at K1, the appendix overstates the domain of the time-indexed formalism.
findings.evidence: The appendix includes K1 in the time-indexed operator family. The K1 chapter says time does not exist at K1 and that tau(K1) is undefined and unrepresentable. Those two statements are only compatible if the appendix explicitly marks t as a formal parameter rather than intrinsic time, which it does not.
findings.required_action: Either state that t is only a formal evolution parameter at K1, or move the lower bound of the time-indexed operator family to K2 where time is said to emerge.

findings.claim: The notation table overloads tau: the tau(K) entry treats it as temporal structure or a temporal-parameter family, but the same item later reuses bare tau as the legacy alias for the topological pair (X,tau). In the K1 module, tau already names the structural topology of K1 while tau(K1) is later declared undefined, so the appendix never disambiguates the temporal and topological meanings.
findings.evidence: The file first assigns tau(K) a temporal meaning and then says topology may be written as (X,tau). The K1 chapter separately defines K1 = (X, tau, mu, A1) with tau as topology and later says tau(K1) is undefined and unrepresentable. That is a real symbol collision, not just a stylistic choice.
findings.required_action: Use a distinct symbol for topology or add an explicit disambiguation note stating that the topological tau is unrelated to the temporal tau(K).
